stories.headline: Court ruling voids CHP congress, ousting Özel and reinstating Kılıçdaroğlu; party splits amid mass protests and rival rallies
stories.summary: An Istanbul appellate court issued a 'mutlak butlan' (absolute nullity) ruling invalidating CHP's November 2023 congress, removing Özgür Özel from the party leadership and reinstating Kemal Kılıçdaroğlu. Police forcibly cleared CHP headquarters; Özel moved operations to parliament while Kılıçdaroğlu held rallies at the general center. Tens of thousands marched in Ankara and İzmir for Özel; 221 former CHP MPs jointly rejected the ruling; Özel's MYK announced signature collection for an extraordinary congress starting June 1; IBB council members, Dilek İmamoğlu, and DEM/İYİ party leaders sided with Özel; European press called it a judicial coup; polls showed Özel beating Erdoğan in a runoff; Kılıçdaroğlu announced a new MYK and implied he would name a presidential candidate; CHP's own website removed leadership rosters.

stories.headline: Foreign Minister Fidan gives wide-ranging interview signaling US-Iran deal imminent, Israel normalization conditions, and Turkey-Japan defense ties
stories.summary: Foreign Minister Hakan Fidan granted an interview to Nikkei Asia covering several diplomatic fronts: he said a US-Iran deal is 'closer than ever,' with Hormuz Strait security the primary focus rather than nuclear issues; he outlined conditions for Turkey-Israel normalization (recognition of a Palestinian state on 1967 borders); he proposed a regional security architecture including Turkey, Pakistan, Saudi Arabia, Egypt, and Gulf states; and he announced Turkey's readiness for joint UAV development and production with Japan. He also said NATO summit preparations in Ankara are proceeding with Trump as expected guest.

stories.headline: TCMB June 11 rate decision awaited; markets focus on inflation data and July wage increases after holiday break
stories.summary: Following the nine-day Eid holiday, Turkish financial markets and media turned to a dense economic calendar: the TCMB Monetary Policy Committee is set to announce its fourth rate decision of the year on June 11; the policy rate currently stands at 37%. TCMB's May market participant survey put year-end inflation expectations at 28.94%, with a projected July salary adjustment of around 18.58% for SSK/Bağ-Kur pensioners. Separately, JPMorgan closed its TL positions citing early-election risk.

stories.headline: Cabinet convenes post-holiday with 'Terror-Free Turkey,' economy, and foreign policy on agenda
stories.summary: After a nine-day Eid holiday, the Presidential Cabinet reconvened under Erdoğan at Beştepe on June 1. Multiple outlets previewed the meeting's agenda: the 'Terörsüz Türkiye' (Terror-Free Turkey) peace process, the economic program, and regional foreign policy developments including the US-Iran war situation were flagged as top items; Erdoğan was expected to make a public statement afterward.

stories.headline: AKP considering minimum pension hike to 36,000 TL and early election scenario
stories.summary: Reports citing AKP party sources indicate the government is working on a social support package that would raise the minimum pension to 36,000 TL in October, aimed at stemming voter erosion among retirees ahead of a potential early election. Party circles reportedly discussed whether such a move could precede an early election call, noting that an election held at least one year ahead of schedule would allow Erdoğan to stand as a candidate again under the constitution.

stories.headline: Erdoğan seeks bilateral meeting with Trump around Turkey-USA World Cup match in Los Angeles
stories.summary: Bloomberg reported that President Erdoğan is seeking to arrange a bilateral meeting with President Trump before or around the Turkey-USA FIFA World Cup Group Stage match scheduled for June 25/26 at SoFi Stadium in Los Angeles. Sources said Erdoğan is also planning to attend the match itself.

stories.headline: Erdoğan phones Algerian President Tebbune on cooperation in trade, energy, and defense
stories.summary: President Erdoğan held a phone call with Algerian President Abdülmecid Tebbune, during which he said Turkey is working to advance bilateral cooperation across all areas, particularly trade, energy, and defense industry. Erdoğan also reiterated Turkey's commitment to regional peace and stability.

stories.headline: DEM Party presses for framework legislation on peace process; AKP awaits MİT field report
stories.summary: DEM Party's İmralı delegation member Pervin Buldan called for a 7-8 clause 'framework law' covering PKK members to be passed before parliament closes. However, AKP sources indicated any legislative steps are contingent on field developments and a forthcoming MİT assessment of whether PKK disarmament is proceeding at the required level. Separately, Bahçeli extended an apology-by-proxy to AKP MP Ensarioğlu, whom he had once branded a 'traitor' for pro-Kurdish peace views that MHP now endorses.

stories.headline: MİT Intelligence Academy publishes analysis on EU free trade strategy and risks to Turkish industry
stories.summary: The National Intelligence Academy (MİA), affiliated with MİT, published an analysis titled 'EU's Free Trade Strategy and Turkey,' examining the EU's new-generation trade agreements with India, MERCOSUR, and Australia. The report warns that these agreements could asymmetrically harm Turkish automotive, textile, and agricultural sectors, and emphasizes updating Turkey's Customs Union agreement as a priority.

stories.headline: Erdoğan gives Eid prayer at Çamlıca Mosque, delivers unity message and congratulates Islamic world
stories.summary: President Erdoğan performed Eid al-Adha prayers at the Grand Çamlıca Mosque in Istanbul, delivering remarks to congregants emphasizing unity and solidarity. He also phoned border troops and Mecca pilgrims, and donated his sacrificial animal via TDV to be slaughtered in Ethiopia for distribution to those in need.

stories.headline: Erdoğan marks 573rd anniversary of Istanbul's conquest with speech warning critics of the city's status
stories.summary: President Erdoğan spoke at the 573rd anniversary event for the Ottoman conquest of Istanbul, declaring that some people still cannot accept the conquest after 573 years. His remarks were interpreted as a response to debates over Istanbul's political status, including ongoing tensions around the city's CHP-led mayor. Bahçeli also released a written message on the anniversary.

stories.headline: Denizli bus crash kills 8; Uzbek president sends condolences to Erdoğan
stories.summary: A bus crash in Sarayköy district of Denizli province killed 8 people. Uzbekistan's President Shavkat Mirziyoyev sent a condolence message to President Erdoğan expressing deep sorrow over the casualties.

stories.summary: Gendarmerie Warrant Officer Yusuf Ergün was killed in a traffic accident on the Ankara-Niğde motorway while on duty. President Erdoğan sent a condolence message to his family.

stories.headline: İBB trial of 414 defendants including İmamoğlu resumes after nine-day holiday break
stories.summary: The Istanbul Metropolitan Municipality (İBB) corruption trial, involving 414 defendants including jailed IBB Mayor and CHP presidential candidate Ekrem İmamoğlu, resumed at Silivri after the nine-day holiday recess. Defense statements were expected to continue and new rulings on pretrial detention were anticipated.

stories.headline: MİT chief Kalın describes Turkey as a crisis-mediation actor; speaks at defense university
stories.summary: MİT Director İbrahim Kalın spoke at the National Defense University, describing Turkey as a country that has moved beyond regional actor status to one that is invited to conflict resolution tables. He referenced PKK disarmament milestones and Turkey's mediation role in the US-Israel-Iran war context. Separately, Kalın was announced to attend a 'Young Turkey Forum' event in Kayseri with Bilal Erdoğan.

stories.headline: NATO July summit preparations in Ankara advance; security measures and civil servant leave announced
stories.summary: Ankara is preparing to host the 36th NATO Leaders Summit on July 7-8. Interior Minister Çiftçi chaired a security planning meeting at the ministry. Separately, it was reported that public employees in nine Ankara districts will be granted leave during the summit period. Commentary noted NATO Secretary-General Rutte had highlighted Turkey's defense capabilities as indispensable to European security.

stories.headline: DEM Party plans autumn congress with possible name change; announces preparatory commission
stories.summary: DEM Party deputy co-chair Mahfuz Güleryüz said the party's planned ordinary congress, scheduled for late September to October, would be open to debating a name change, revisions to the party program and statute, and new leadership. The party framed the congress as part of a new 'Peace and Democratic Society' period.
